sources.title: Baidu frontend interview note longest-palindromic-substring prompt
Fresh center-expansion vs brute-force oracle validation

claims.text: The source identifies longest palindromic substring (LeetCode 5); no language or equal-length tie rule is preserved.
Enumerating character and gap centers covers odd and even palindromes, with O(n^2) worst-case expansion and constant auxiliary state.
The exact implementation matches an independent brute-force earliest-tie oracle on seven fixed and 5000 deterministic randomized strings.

validation.reported_stdout: PASS fixed=7 randomized=5000 oracle=bruteforce earliest-tie=true odd-even=true empty-null=true

boundary_tests.expected: bab under explicit earliest-start tie rule
exact match with independent brute-force earliest-tie oracle

findings: The repository source recoverably identifies longest palindromic substring (LeetCode 5) without preserving a language or equal-length tie rule.
The candidate explicitly labels earliest-start tie-breaking as an implementation choice rather than a source requirement.
Both character centers and character-gap centers are enumerated, covering odd and even palindrome lengths.
The Java candidate is a complete runnable class and its boundary arithmetic uses left+1/right-1 after expansion.
Seven fixed cases and 5000 deterministic randomized strings agree exactly with an independent O(n^3) brute-force oracle under the same tie rule.
The candidate states O(n^2) worst-case time and O(1) auxiliary state and does not misclassify center expansion as linear time.
No generic long-tail placeholder implementation or fabricated project experience remains.
